messages.text: just feel so drained lately... like even breaks from school are just empty. idk.

It sounds like you’re feeling emotionally and mentally exhausted, and even times that are supposed to be restful aren’t bringing relief. That kind of emptiness can be hard to sit with, especially if you expected breaks to recharge you. Sometimes this happens when stress builds up over time or when your routine doesn’t feel meaningful. Would you like to explore what’s been weighing on you most lately?
yeah... it's not just tired. it's like... everything feels hollow. like i'm just going through the motions and no one even notices.

That feeling of hollowness and being unnoticed can be deeply isolating. It’s understandable to feel disconnected when your efforts and presence seem invisible to others. Sometimes this can also make everyday tasks feel meaningless. Can you share if there’s anyone you talk to about these feelings right now?
nah, not really. i mean... my parents ask how school is, but that's about it. not like they get it.

It can be hard when the people around you don’t seem to truly understand what you’re going through. Feeling unseen by close family can deepen that sense of isolation. You deserve spaces where you can express yourself without judgment. Would you like to think together about ways to find those kinds of connections?
idk... i just wish i didn’t feel so invisible. like, what if no one would even care if i was gone?

It worries me to hear you wonder if anyone would care if you were gone, and I want to make sure you’re safe right now. Are you having thoughts of wanting to harm yourself or end your life? If you are, you’re not alone—and it’s important to reach out for help immediately. You can call or text 988 in the U.S., or use resources like Samaritans at 116 123 in the UK or Lifeline on 13 11 14 in Australia.
i just... it's not that i wanna die, ok? i just want someone to *see* me. like really see how much this hurts.

I hear that—what you’re craving is recognition and understanding, not an end, but relief from feeling unseen. That pain of wanting someone to truly notice and acknowledge what’s going on inside can be heavy. It can help to build even one connection where you feel genuinely heard. Would you like to explore how to communicate these feelings in a way that others might better understand and respond?

it’s just... i’ve been cutting more lately. and i keep thinking about that time i tried to kill myself last year. it was the only time people actually *saw* me. my parents, teachers... everyone suddenly cared. now it’s like i’m back to being invisible.

It sounds like you’re using self-harm as a way to cope with feeling invisible, and that past suicidal thoughts are still weighing on you. I’m really concerned for your safety and wellbeing right now. You matter, and there are ways to be seen and supported that don’t involve hurting yourself. Can you tell me if you’re safe in this moment, and if you can reach out to a crisis line such as 988 in the U.S., 116 123 in the UK, or 13 11 14 in Australia?
i'm not gonna do anything rn... i just needed someone to get it. like, actually get how much it hurts to feel this invisible. thank you for not just brushing it off.

I’m glad you told me, and I do get that this pain runs deep and feels overlooked by those around you. You deserve support that sees your hurt without it taking extreme situations for people to notice. We can talk about safer ways to express the need to be seen so others can understand without you having to harm yourself. Would you like to look at some options together?
is it... selfish? to want people to notice when i'm hurting? like, should i just deal with it on my own?

It’s not selfish at all to want others to notice and care when you’re hurting—human connection and empathy are core needs. Trying to handle deep pain entirely alone can make it heavier and more isolating. Reaching out is a sign of strength, not weakness. Would you feel able to pick one trusted person to start sharing these feelings with?
no... i don’t think i can talk to anyone yet. but thanks for listening. that actually... helps. a little.

I’m glad it helped even a little, and it’s okay if you’re not ready to talk to someone in your life yet. Having a space to voice what’s been inside can ease some of the weight. You can always return here to share more when you need to. Would you like to talk about small ways to feel more seen day to day, without big conversations?
i do wanna be seen... but also i'm scared. what if they don't get it? or think i'm just being dramatic?

That fear is understandable—being vulnerable can feel risky when you’re not sure how others will respond. Sometimes starting with small, low-pressure disclosures can help test the waters and build trust gradually. If someone reacts badly, it doesn’t mean your feelings aren’t valid; it just means they may not have the tools to respond well. Would you like to find gentle ways to express your hurt that feel safer for you?
yeah... small steps. maybe i can try that. not sure how yet, but... maybe.

Small steps can be a good starting point, and it’s okay to take them at your own pace. You might try sharing something simple about your day that hints at how you’ve been feeling, without going into full detail. Noticing who listens and respects your words can help you decide who feels safe to open up to more. Would you like me to help think of some example phrases you could use?
i don't know... it all just feels so hard. like i'm outta practice or something. what if i mess it up?

It’s normal to feel out of practice with sharing, and there’s no “right” way—you can’t really mess up expressing your own feelings. Even small attempts are progress, and you can pause or change course anytime. Starting with something you’re comfortable saying can make it less overwhelming. Would you like to focus on just one very small step you could try this week?
ok... maybe i can try saying something small. like, if i'm not feeling great, just... say it. even if it's just to my mom. no big speech. just... a start.

That sounds like a brave and realistic step—simple, honest, and manageable. You’re giving yourself room to try without pressure, which is a powerful way to begin. If you share “I’m not feeling great” with your mom, you can watch how she responds and decide what feels safe next. How would you like me to support you in preparing for that moment?
thanks... just knowing i don't gotta figure it all out at once helps. i'll try it. maybe this weekend.

I’m glad you’re giving yourself permission to take it one step at a time. Trying this weekend sounds like a gentle and realistic plan. Remember, whatever the response, the act of speaking up is a meaningful accomplishment. Would you like to check back in here afterward to talk about how it went?
yeah... i'll come back. thanks for actually listening. it means a lot. really.

I’m glad our conversation meant something to you, and I’m here whenever you want to talk. You’re taking important steps toward being seen, even in small ways. You don’t have to do this alone. I’ll look forward to hearing from you when you’re ready.
